neighbours.label: 'than' / 'compared (to)' introducing the comparison group in a health or research finding
fire: Children who slept less were twice as likely to be overweight than those who slept well.
Runners had lower blood pressure than adults who did no exercise.
Patients on the new drug recovered faster than patients given a placebo.
When compared to non-smokers, smokers had higher rates of gum disease.
Teenagers who skipped breakfast scored worse than classmates who ate.
Night-shift workers reported more headaches than people who worked days.
Mothers who breastfed had a lower risk of diabetes compared with mothers who did not.
Older drivers were less likely to crash than younger drivers in the survey.
quiet: Children who slept less were often tired during morning lessons.
Runners in the study had their blood pressure measured each week.
Patients on the new drug recovered at home within two weeks.
Among smokers, gum disease was a frequent complaint at the clinic.
Teenagers who skipped breakfast often bought snacks at school.
Night-shift workers reported frequent headaches in the survey.
Mothers who breastfed were asked about their diet in the study.
Older drivers in the survey said they avoided driving at night.
